claim: Preterm birth is the leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality worldwide.
source: Preterm birth is the leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality worldwide.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific consensus about the global impact of preterm birth on neonatal health outcomes.

claim: Most cases of preterm birth occur spontaneously and result from preterm labor with intact (spontaneous preterm labor [sPTL]) or ruptured (preterm prelabor rupture of membranes [PPROM]) membranes.
source: Most cases of preterm birth occur spontaneously and result from preterm labor with intact (spontaneous preterm labor [sPTL]) or ruptured (preterm prelabor rupture of membranes [PPROM]) membranes.
evidence: This statement is supported by established knowledge in the field and is cited in the introduction with references to prior literature.

claim: Throughout uncomplicated gestation, the vaginal immunoproteome harbors a cytokine network with a homeostatic profile.
source: Throughout uncomplicated gestation, the vaginal immunoproteome harbors a cytokine network with a homeostatic profile.
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 2 showing gestational age-dependent changes in immune mediators during normal pregnancy.

claim: The vaginal immunoproteome is skewed toward a pro-inflammatory state in pregnant women who ultimately experience sPTL and PPROM.
source: Yet, the vaginal immunoproteome is skewed toward a pro-inflammatory state in pregnant women who ultimately experience sPTL and PPROM.
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Figures 3-6 showing increased pro-inflammatory cytokines in women with sPTB compared to controls.

claim: The inflammatory profile in sPTB includes increased monocyte chemoattractants.
source: Such an inflammatory profile includes increased monocyte chemoattractants, cytokines indicative of macrophage and T-cell activation, and reduced antimicrobial proteins/peptides.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4 showing increased CCL2, CCL3, and CCL4 in women with sPTB.

claim: The inflammatory profile in sPTB includes cytokines indicative of macrophage activation.
source: Such an inflammatory profile includes increased monocyte chemoattractants, cytokines indicative of macrophage and T-cell activation, and reduced antimicrobial proteins/peptides.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4 supplement 1 showing changes in macrophage-associated cytokines like IL-12p70 and IL-15.

claim: The inflammatory profile in sPTB includes cytokines indicative of T-cell activation.
source: Such an inflammatory profile includes increased monocyte chemoattractants, cytokines indicative of macrophage and T-cell activation, and reduced antimicrobial proteins/peptides.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 5 showing increased T-cell-associated cytokines like IL-2, IL-10, IL-4, and IL-17A in sPTB cases.

claim: The inflammatory profile in sPTB includes reduced antimicrobial proteins/peptides.
source: Such an inflammatory profile includes increased monocyte chemoattractants, cytokines indicative of macrophage and T-cell activation, and reduced antimicrobial proteins/peptides.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 6 showing decreased SLPI and β-defensin-2 in early PPROM cases.

claim: The vaginal immunoproteome has improved predictive value over maternal characteristics alone for identifying women at risk for early (<34 weeks) sPTB.
source: The vaginal immunoproteome has improved predictive value over maternal characteristics alone for identifying women at risk for early (<34 weeks) sPTB.
evidence: This is supported by predictive modeling data shown in Figure 7, particularly for early PPROM.

claim: Preterm birth afflicts 1 of every 10 children born worldwide.
source: Preterm birth, defined as live birth before 37 weeks of gestation (American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, 2021), afflicts 1 of every 10 children born worldwide (Chawanpaiboon et al., 2019; Martin and Hamilton, 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to epidemiological studies.

claim: The economic burden of preterm birth amounts to more than $25.2 billion in healthcare costs annually in the United States alone.
source: The economic burden of preterm birth amounts to more than $25.2 billion in healthcare costs annually in the United States alone (Waitzman et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to an economic analysis study.

claim: Two-thirds of preterm births occur spontaneously.
source: Two-thirds of preterm births occur spontaneously (i.e., spontaneous preterm birth [sPTB]) (Goldenberg et al., 2008), while the remainder are due to evident clinical conditions (e.g., preeclampsia and intrauterine growth restriction) that jeopardize maternal–fetal well-being and require medically indicated delivery (i.e., iatrogenic preterm birth) (Goldenberg et al., 2008; Romero et al., 2014a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a review article.

claim: The pathogenesis of sPTL and PPROM can include local inflammatory processes.
source: The pathogenesis of sPTL and PPROM can include local inflammatory processes (Romero et al., 2014a); yet, each is considered a syndrome with distinct underlying mechanisms of disease (Goldenberg et al., 2008; Romero et al., 2014a) and thus requiring different clinical managements (American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, 2016; Dvorakova and Ivankova, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to review articles and clinical guidelines.

claim: sPTL and PPROM are considered syndromes with distinct underlying mechanisms of disease.
source: The pathogenesis of sPTL and PPROM can include local inflammatory processes (Romero et al., 2014a); yet, each is considered a syndrome with distinct underlying mechanisms of disease (Goldenberg et al., 2008; Romero et al., 2014a) and thus requiring different clinical managements (American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, 2016; Dvorakova and Ivankova, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: Women with a sonographic short cervix (≤ 25 mm) are sixfold more likely to deliver a preterm neonate.
source: Yet, to date, assessment of cervical length remains the strongest and most cost-effective predictor of sPTB: women with a sonographic short cervix (≤ 25 mm) are sixfold more likely to deliver a preterm neonate (Iams et al., 1996), and tailored treatment with natural progesterone reduces such risk by half (Fonseca et al., 2007; Hassan et al., 2011; Romero et al., 2014b; Romero et al., 2016; Romero et al., 2017; Conde-Agudelo et al., 2018; Romero et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a clinical study.

claim: Tailored treatment with natural progesterone reduces the risk of preterm birth by half in women with short cervix.
source: Yet, to date, assessment of cervical length remains the strongest and most cost-effective predictor of sPTB: women with a sonographic short cervix (≤ 25 mm) are sixfold more likely to deliver a preterm neonate (Iams et al., 1996), and tailored treatment with natural progesterone reduces such risk by half (Fonseca et al., 2007; Hassan et al., 2011; Romero et al., 2014b; Romero et al., 2016; Romero et al., 2017; Conde-Agudelo et al., 2018; Romero et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to clinical trials.

claim: This study represents the largest (N = 739 women, n = 2819 samples) and most comprehensive (31 immune mediators) profiling of the soluble immune response in vaginal fluid throughout well-characterized pregnancies.
source: This study represents the largest (N = 739 women, n = 2819 samples) and most comprehensive (31 immune mediators) profiling of the soluble immune response in vaginal fluid throughout well-characterized pregnancies that culminated in the delivery of a term neonate (controls) or those that resulted in sPTB (sPTL and PPROM cases) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the study design and sample size described in the methods and shown in Figure 1.

claim: The study population was primarily composed of African-American women with an average body mass index (BMI) of 28.7 kg/m2.
source: Of note, this study addressed a high-risk population primarily composed of African-American women with an average body mass index (BMI) of 28.7 kg/m2.
evidence: This is supported by demographic data presented in Table 1.

claim: The vaginal concentrations of IL-1β declined as gestation progressed in normal pregnancy.
source: Specifically, the vaginal concentrations of IL-1β (Figure 2), IL-1α (Figure 2B), CXCL8 (Figure 2C), IL-2 (Figure 2D), IL-12/IL-23p40 (Figure 2E), GM-CSF (Figure 2F), and β-defensin-2 (Figure 2G) declined as gestation progressed.
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The vaginal concentrations of IL-1α declined as gestation progressed in normal pregnancy.
source: Specifically, the vaginal concentrations of IL-1β (Figure 2), IL-1α (Figure 2B), CXCL8 (Figure 2C), IL-2 (Figure 2D), IL-12/IL-23p40 (Figure 2E), GM-CSF (Figure 2F), and β-defensin-2 (Figure 2G) declined as gestation progressed.
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The vaginal concentrations of CXCL8 declined as gestation progressed in normal pregnancy.
source: Specifically, the vaginal concentrations of IL-1β (Figure 2), IL-1α (Figure 2B), CXCL8 (Figure 2C), IL-2 (Figure 2D), IL-12/IL-23p40 (Figure 2E), GM-CSF (Figure 2F), and β-defensin-2 (Figure 2G) declined as gestation progressed.
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The vaginal concentrations of IL-2 declined as gestation progressed in normal pregnancy.
source: Specifically, the vaginal concentrations of IL-1β (Figure 2), IL-1α (Figure 2B), CXCL8 (Figure 2C), IL-2 (Figure 2D), IL-12/IL-23p40 (Figure 2E), GM-CSF (Figure 2F), and β-defensin-2 (Figure 2G) declined as gestation progressed.

claim: The vaginal concentrations of IL-12/IL-23p40 declined as gestation progressed in normal pregnancy.
source: Specifically, the vaginal concentrations of IL-1β (Figure 2), IL-1α (Figure 2B), CXCL8 (Figure 2C), IL-2 (Figure 2D), IL-12/IL-23p40 (Figure 2E), GM-CSF (Figure 2F), and β-defensin-2 (Figure 2G) declined as gestation progressed.

claim: The vaginal concentrations of GM-CSF declined as gestation progressed in normal pregnancy.
source: Specifically, the vaginal concentrations of IL-1β (Figure 2), IL-1α (Figure 2B), CXCL8 (Figure 2C), IL-2 (Figure 2D), IL-12/IL-23p40 (Figure 2E), GM-CSF (Figure 2F), and β-defensin-2 (Figure 2G) declined as gestation progressed.

claim: The vaginal concentrations of β-defensin-2 declined as gestation progressed in normal pregnancy.
source: Specifically, the vaginal concentrations of IL-1β (Figure 2), IL-1α (Figure 2B), CXCL8 (Figure 2C), IL-2 (Figure 2D), IL-12/IL-23p40 (Figure 2E), GM-CSF (Figure 2F), and β-defensin-2 (Figure 2G) declined as gestation progressed.

claim: CCL17 increased with gestational age in normal pregnancy.
source: On the other hand, CCL17 (Figure 2H), CXCL10 (Figure 2I), and VEGF (Figure 2J) increased with gestational age.
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: CXCL10 increased with gestational age in normal pregnancy.
source: On the other hand, CCL17 (Figure 2H), CXCL10 (Figure 2I), and VEGF (Figure 2J) increased with gestational age.
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 2I.

claim: VEGF increased with gestational age in normal pregnancy.
source: On the other hand, CCL17 (Figure 2H), CXCL10 (Figure 2I), and VEGF (Figure 2J) increased with gestational age.
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 2J.

claim: IL-6 was increased in women who ultimately experienced sPTB compared to those who delivered at term.
source: Notably, two pro-inflammatory cytokines that have been considered master regulators of parturition, IL-6 (Romero et al., 2006a; Robertson et al., 2010; Gomez‐Lopez et al., 2016) and IL-1β (Romero et al., 1989; Romero et al., 1992a), were increased in women who ultimately experienced sPTB compared to those who delivered at term (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: IL-1β was increased in women who ultimately experienced sPTB compared to those who delivered at term.
source: Notably, two pro-inflammatory cytokines that have been considered master regulators of parturition, IL-6 (Romero et al., 2006a; Robertson et al., 2010; Gomez‐Lopez et al., 2016) and IL-1β (Romero et al., 1989; Romero et al., 1992a), were increased in women who ultimately experienced sPTB compared to those who delivered at term (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: IL-6 was increased in both sPTL and PPROM subsets compared to women who delivered at term.
source: We observed that IL-6 and IL-1β were increased in both sPTB subsets compared to women who delivered at term (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: IL-1β was increased in both sPTL and PPROM subsets compared to women who delivered at term.
source: We observed that IL-6 and IL-1β were increased in both sPTB subsets compared to women who delivered at term (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: IL-16 was increased in late sPTL and early PPROM.
source: Likewise, IL-16, a pro-inflammatory mediator (Chupp et al., 1998) reported in the female reproductive tract (FRT) (Athayde et al., 2000; Florova et al., 2021), was also increased in late sPTL and early PPROM (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The vaginal concentrations of CXCL8 (high-affinity, HA) were increased in women with sPTB compared to term controls.
source: The vaginal concentrations of CXCL8 (high-affinity, HA), TNF, and IFN-γ, immune mediators previously reported in the vaginal fluid with conflicting results (Imseis et al., 1997; Wennerholm et al., 1998; Donders et al., 2003; Kalinka et al., 2005; Chandiramani et al., 2012; Kacerovsky et al., 2015; Jung et al., 2016; Yoo et al., 2017; Short et al., 2018; Mikołajczyk et al., 2020; Short et al., 2021; Chan et al., 2022; Grewal et al., 2022), were also increased in women with sPTB compared to term controls (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The vaginal concentrations of TNF were increased in women with sPTB compared to term controls.
source: The vaginal concentrations of CXCL8 (high-affinity, HA), TNF, and IFN-γ, immune mediators previously reported in the vaginal fluid with conflicting results (Imseis et al., 1997; Wennerholm et al., 1998; Donders et al., 2003; Kalinka et al., 2005; Chandiramani et al., 2012; Kacerovsky et al., 2015; Jung et al., 2016; Yoo et al., 2017; Short et al., 2018; Mikołajczyk et al., 2020; Short et al., 2021; Chan et al., 2022; Grewal et al., 2022), were also increased in women with sPTB compared to term controls (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The vaginal concentrations of IFN-γ were increased in women with sPTB compared to term controls.
source: The vaginal concentrations of CXCL8 (high-affinity, HA), TNF, and IFN-γ, immune mediators previously reported in the vaginal fluid with conflicting results (Imseis et al., 1997; Wennerholm et al., 1998; Donders et al., 2003; Kalinka et al., 2005; Chandiramani et al., 2012; Kacerovsky et al., 2015; Jung et al., 2016; Yoo et al., 2017; Short et al., 2018; Mikołajczyk et al., 2020; Short et al., 2021; Chan et al., 2022; Grewal et al., 2022), were also increased in women with sPTB compared to term controls (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The elevation in CXCL8 (HA), TNF, and IFN-γ appeared to be driven by late sPTL cases.
source: Yet, such elevation appeared to be driven by late sPTL cases (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by subgroup analysis data shown in Figure 3D-F.

claim: CCL2 was increased in women with sPTB compared to those who delivered at term.
source: Interestingly, each of these chemokines followed the same pattern: these mediators were increased in women with sPTB compared to those who delivered at term (Figure 4B–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: CCL3 was increased in women with sPTB compared to those who delivered at term.
source: Interestingly, each of these chemokines followed the same pattern: these mediators were increased in women with sPTB compared to those who delivered at term (Figure 4B–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: CCL4 was increased in women with sPTB compared to those who delivered at term.
source: Interestingly, each of these chemokines followed the same pattern: these mediators were increased in women with sPTB compared to those who delivered at term (Figure 4B–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: CCL2 was increased in women with late sPTL and those with early PPROM.
source: Specifically, CCL2 and CCL3 were increased in women with late sPTL and those with early PPROM (Figure 4B and C), and CCL4 was increased in early and late sPTL as well as in early PPROM (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by subgroup analysis data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: CCL3 was increased in women with late sPTL and those with early PPROM.
source: Specifically, CCL2 and CCL3 were increased in women with late sPTL and those with early PPROM (Figure 4B and C), and CCL4 was increased in early and late sPTL as well as in early PPROM (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by subgroup analysis data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: CCL4 was increased in early and late sPTL as well as in early PPROM.
source: Specifically, CCL2 and CCL3 were increased in women with late sPTL and those with early PPROM (Figure 4B and C), and CCL4 was increased in early and late sPTL as well as in early PPROM (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by subgroup analysis data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: IL-12p70 was increased in both all and late sPTL cases, but not in other subsets of sPTB.
source: Specifically, the pro-inflammatory IL-12p70 (Ethuin et al., 2003; Taylor et al., 2013) was increased in both all and late sPTL cases, but not in other subsets of sPTB (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 4 supplement 1B.

claim: IL-12/IL-23p40 was increased only in early PPROM among the sPTB subsets.
source: By contrast, the anti-inflammatory IL-12/IL-23p40 (Mattner et al., 1993; Kato et al., 1996) was increased only in early PPROM among the sPTB subsets (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 4 supplement 1C.

claim: The vaginal concentrations of IL-15 were increased in late sPTL as well as in early PPROM.
source: Yet, the vaginal concentrations of IL-15 were increased in late sPTL as well as in early PPROM (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 4 supplement 1D.

claim: The vaginal concentrations of IL-2 were increased in women with sPTB; specifically, in those with late sPTL, but not in women with PPROM.
source: The vaginal concentrations of IL-2 and IL-10 were increased in women with sPTB; specifically, in those with late sPTL, but not in women with PPROM (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The vaginal concentrations of IL-10 were increased in women with sPTB; specifically, in those with late sPTL, but not in women with PPROM.
source: The vaginal concentrations of IL-2 and IL-10 were increased in women with sPTB; specifically, in those with late sPTL, but not in women with PPROM (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The vaginal concentrations of IL-4 were increased in specific subsets of sPTB (late sPTL and early PPROM).
source: In addition, the vaginal concentrations of IL-4 and IL-17A were increased in specific subsets of sPTB (late sPTL and early PPROM) (Figure 5D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The vaginal concentrations of IL-17A were increased in specific subsets of sPTB (late sPTL and early PPROM).
source: In addition, the vaginal concentrations of IL-4 and IL-17A were increased in specific subsets of sPTB (late sPTL and early PPROM) (Figure 5D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The vaginal concentrations of both SLPI and β-defensin-2 were decreased in early PPROM.
source: Notably, the vaginal concentrations of both SLPI and β-defensin-2 were decreased in early PPROM (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 6B and C.

claim: The vaginal concentrations of GM-CSF were only increased in early PPROM.
source: While the vaginal concentrations of GM-CSF were only increased in early PPROM (Figure 6D), VEGF was decreased in women with early and late sPTL and early PPROM (Figure 6E).
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: VEGF was decreased in women with early and late sPTL and early PPROM.
source: While the vaginal concentrations of GM-CSF were only increased in early PPROM (Figure 6D), VEGF was decreased in women with early and late sPTL and early PPROM (Figure 6E).
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The vaginal immunoproteome has the highest potential predictive value for early PPROM <34 (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.787).
source: When considering the vaginal concentrations of cytokines, chemokines, growth factors, and defensins without including maternal characteristics (black line), the vaginal immunoproteome has the highest potential predictive value for early PPROM <34 (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.787) (Figure 7E), with the two most informative immune mediators for the prediction of early PPROM being VEGF and IL-1β.
evidence: This claim is supported by random forest modeling data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: The two most informative immune mediators for the prediction of early PPROM are VEGF and IL-1β.
source: When considering the vaginal concentrations of cytokines, chemokines, growth factors, and defensins without including maternal characteristics (black line), the vaginal immunoproteome has the highest potential predictive value for early PPROM <34 (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.787) (Figure 7E), with the two most informative immune mediators for the prediction of early PPROM being VEGF and IL-1β.
evidence: This claim is supported by feature importance analysis from random forest modeling shown in Figure 7E.

claim: For early sPTL, concentrations of IL-1β, IL-16, and IL-13 were most informative.
source: For early sPTL, concentrations of IL-1β, IL-16, and IL-13 were most informative.
evidence: This claim is supported by feature importance analysis from random forest modeling.

claim: When maternal characteristics were included in the models with all vaginal analytes, the prediction accuracy of models predicting sPTB, and the subsets of all sPTL cases and all PPROM cases, was improved.
source: When maternal characteristics (maternal age, BMI, parity, and history of preterm birth) were included in the models with all vaginal analytes (red line), the prediction accuracy of models predicting sPTB, and the subsets of all sPTL cases and all PPROM cases, was improved (p<0.05 for all) (Figure 7A, B, and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of random forest models with and without maternal characteristics shown in Figure 7A, B, and D.

claim: The prediction of early sPTL and early PPROM was not improved with the addition of maternal characteristics to the predictive model.
source: On the other hand, the prediction of early sPTL (Figure 7C) and early PPROM (Figure 7E) was not improved with the addition of maternal characteristics to the predictive model.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of random forest models with and without maternal characteristics shown in Figure 7C and E.

claim: Immune mediator data and maternal characteristics resulted in significantly improved prediction of PPROM <34 (DeLong test p<0.023).
source: Immune mediator data and maternal characteristics resulted in significantly improved prediction of PPROM <34 (DeLong test p<0.023) and led to higher point estimates for all other outcomes when using the last sample before 28 weeks (Figure 7).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical comparison of predictive models shown in Figure 7.

claim: IL-6 is a highly pleiotropic cytokine that participates in acute and chronic inflammation, hematopoiesis, and other developmental and physiological processes.
source: Interleukin-6 is a highly pleiotropic cytokine that participates in acute and chronic inflammation, hematopoiesis, and other developmental and physiological processes (Jones and Jenkins, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a review article.

claim: IL-6 not only regulates the innate immune response but also participates in the transition to a sustained adaptive immune response.
source: Importantly, IL-6 not only regulates the innate immune response but also participates in the transition to a sustained adaptive immune response, which has made this cytokine and its family attractive targets for immunotherapies (Jones and Jenkins, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a review article.

claim: IL-6 is the established biomarker for the diagnosis of acute intra-amniotic inflammation.
source: Indeed, IL-6 is the established biomarker for the diagnosis of acute intra-amniotic inflammation (Yoon et al., 2001), the most well-established causal link to preterm labor and birth (Romero et al., 2006b; Romero et al., 2007; Goldenberg et al., 2008; Romero et al., 2014a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to clinical studies.

claim: Acute intra-amniotic inflammation is the most well-established causal link to preterm labor and birth.
source: Indeed, IL-6 is the established biomarker for the diagnosis of acute intra-amniotic inflammation (Yoon et al., 2001), the most well-established causal link to preterm labor and birth (Romero et al., 2006b; Romero et al., 2007; Goldenberg et al., 2008; Romero et al., 2014a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to review articles and clinical studies.

claim: IL-1β is synthesized as a zymogen and requires processing via specific intracellular machinery (i.e., the NLRP3 inflammasome) to be released in its mature and bioactive form.
source: Yet, IL-1β is synthesized as a zymogen and therefore requires processing via specific intracellular machinery (i.e., the NLRP3 inflammasome) to be released in its mature and bioactive form (Kostura et al., 1989).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a study on IL-1β processing and established knowledge of inflammasome biology.

claim: The tissues surrounding the amniotic cavity (i.e., the chorioamniotic membranes), as well as tissues of the upper FRT (e.g., uterine tissues), express the components of the NLRP3 inflammasome.
source: Notably, we have provided in vivo and in vitro demonstrations that the tissues surrounding the amniotic cavity (i.e., the chorioamniotic membranes), as well as tissues of the upper FRT (e.g., uterine tissues), express the components of the NLRP3 inflammasome (Plazyo et al., 2016; Gomez-Lopez et al., 2017; Gomez-Lopez et al., 2018; Gomez-Lopez et al., 2019b; Gomez-Lopez et al., 2019a; Faro et al., 2019; Motomura et al., 2020; Motomura et al., 2021; Motomura et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies by the authors.

claim: In vivo administration of LPS or alarmins results in the processing of active caspase-1 and the subsequent release of mature IL-1β, leading to preterm labor and birth.
source: In fact, in vivo administration of LPS or alarmins, pathogen-associated molecular patterns, and danger-associated molecular patterns that can activate the NLRP3 inflammasome (Swanson et al., 2019) results in the processing of active caspase-1 and the subsequent release of mature IL-1β, leading to preterm labor and birth (Gomez-Lopez et al., 2019b; Faro et al., 2019; Motomura et al., 2020; Motomura et al., 2021; Motomura et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: The intra-amniotic infusion of IL-1β triggers the common pathway of parturition and leads to preterm birth in non-human primates.
source: In line with these results, the intra-amniotic infusion of IL-1β triggers the common pathway of parturition and leads to preterm birth in non-human primates (Gravett et al., 1994; Witkin et al., 1994; Baggia et al., 1996; Vadillo-Ortega et al., 2002; Sadowsky et al., 2006; Presicce et al., 2015) and mice (Yoshimura and Hirsch, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to animal studies.

claim: The intra-amniotic infusion of IL-1β triggers the common pathway of parturition and leads to preterm birth in mice.
source: In line with these results, the intra-amniotic infusion of IL-1β triggers the common pathway of parturition and leads to preterm birth in non-human primates (Gravett et al., 1994; Witkin et al., 1994; Baggia et al., 1996; Vadillo-Ortega et al., 2002; Sadowsky et al., 2006; Presicce et al., 2015) and mice (Yoshimura and Hirsch, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a mouse study.

claim: The blockade of IL-1β through natural inhibitors (e.g., IL-1RA) rescues preterm labor and birth.
source: Moreover, the blockade of either of these pro-inflammatory cytokines through natural inhibitors (e.g., IL-1RA [Romero and Tartakovsky, 1992b]) or neutralizing antibodies (e.g., anti-IL-6R [Wakabayashi et al., 2013; Farias-Jofre et al., 2023]) rescues preterm labor and birth.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: The blockade of IL-6 through neutralizing antibodies (e.g., anti-IL-6R) rescues preterm labor and birth.
source: Moreover, the blockade of either of these pro-inflammatory cytokines through natural inhibitors (e.g., IL-1RA [Romero and Tartakovsky, 1992b]) or neutralizing antibodies (e.g., anti-IL-6R [Wakabayashi et al., 2013; Farias-Jofre et al., 2023]) rescues preterm labor and birth.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: The primary receptor for CCL2 is CCR2, which is predominantly expressed by inflammatory monocytes and controls the trafficking of such cells.
source: The primary receptor for CCL2 is CCR2, which is predominantly expressed by inflammatory monocytes and controls the trafficking of such cells (Griffith et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a review article and established knowledge of chemokine biology.

claim: CCL2/CCR2 interactions are considered to be required for inflammatory monocyte migration into peripheral tissues.
source: CCL2 is rapidly produced by activated tissue or immune cells, and CCL2/CCR2 interactions are considered to be required for inflammatory monocyte migration into peripheral tissues (Kuziel et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to an experimental study.

claim: CCL3 and CCL4 can signal through CCR1 and CCR5, which can be expressed by monocytes and T cells.
source: CCL3 and CCL4 can signal through CCR1 and CCR5, which can be expressed by monocytes and T cells (Griffith et al., 2014; Dyer, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to review articles and established knowledge of chemokine receptor biology.

claim: CCR1 and CCR5 have been demonstrated to promote monocyte adhesion and transmigration in an in vitro setting.
source: CCR1 and CCR5 have been demonstrated to promote monocyte adhesion and transmigration in an in vitro setting (Weber et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to an in vitro study.

claim: Women who ultimately will develop a short cervix displayed a fivefold increase in their vaginal concentrations of CCL2 compared to controls.
source: Moreover, women who ultimately will develop a short cervix, which is a strong predictor of sPTB (Andersen et al., 1990; Iams et al., 1996; Heath et al., 1998; Hassan et al., 2000; Goldenberg et al., 2008; Romero et al., 2014a), displayed a fivefold increase in their vaginal concentrations of CCL2 compared to controls (Chandiramani et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a clinical study.

claim: Defensins are the largest family of AMPs found in humans, comprising small cationic peptides produced by a variety of immune and nonimmune cells.
source: Defensins are the largest family of AMPs found in humans, comprising small cationic peptides produced by a variety of immune and nonimmune cells, and are subdivided into α, β, and θ defensins (Lichtenstein, 1991; Yang et al., 2002; Maisetta et al., 2003; Ganz, 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to review articles and established knowledge of antimicrobial peptide biology.

claim: There are four human β-defensins (HBD-1–4) which are primarily expressed by epithelial cells and have been reported in the FRT.
source: Specifically, there are four human β-defensins (HBD-1–4) which are primarily expressed by epithelial cells and have been reported in the FRT (King et al., 2003; Yarbrough et al., 2015), including the vaginal fluid (Elovitz et al., 2019; Florova et al., 2021) as well as in the gestational tissues (Espinoza et al., 2003; Soto et al., 2007; King et al., 2007; Kim et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: The vaginal concentrations of β-defensin-2 were found to be decreased in women who ultimately underwent sPTB compared to those who delivered at term.
source: Indeed, the vaginal concentrations of β-defensin-2 were found to be decreased in women who ultimately underwent sPTB compared to those who delivered at term (Elovitz et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: Early PPROM has been previously associated with increased rates of neonatal morbidity.
source: Early PPROM has been previously associated with increased rates of neonatal morbidity (Goya et al., 2013; Yu et al., 2015; Pinto et al., 2019) and mortality (Goya et al., 2013; González-Mesa et al., 2021; Yu et al., 2015), thus women at risk for this subset of sPTB represent a target population for the development of predictive and preventive clinical tools.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to clinical studies.

claim: Early PPROM has been previously associated with increased rates of neonatal mortality.
source: Early PPROM has been previously associated with increased rates of neonatal morbidity (Goya et al., 2013; Yu et al., 2015; Pinto et al., 2019) and mortality (Goya et al., 2013; González-Mesa et al., 2021; Yu et al., 2015), thus women at risk for this subset of sPTB represent a target population for the development of predictive and preventive clinical tools.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to clinical studies.

claim: SLPI is a secreted inhibitor that protects host cells against damage from extracellular proteases and is a central player in the constitutive host response in the FRT.
source: SLPI is a secreted inhibitor that protects host cells against damage from extracellular proteases and is a central player in the constitutive host response in the FRT (Hein et al., 2002; Itaoka et al., 2015; Florova et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on SLPI function.

claim: SLPI is negatively correlated with Gemella spp.
source: We previously showed that SLPI is negatively correlated with Gemella spp. (Florova et al., 2021), a member of the vaginal community state type (CST) IV (Ravel et al., 2011) that is linked to increased risk for preterm birth (DiGiulio et al., 2015; Tabatabaei et al., 2019; Elovitz et al., 2019; Hočevar et al., 2019; Chang et al., 2020; Odogwu et al., 2021; Kumar et al., 2021; Dunlop et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a prior study by the authors.

claim: Gemella spp. is a member of the vaginal community state type (CST) IV that is linked to increased risk for preterm birth.
source: We previously showed that SLPI is negatively correlated with Gemella spp. (Florova et al., 2021), a member of the vaginal community state type (CST) IV (Ravel et al., 2011) that is linked to increased risk for preterm birth (DiGiulio et al., 2015; Tabatabaei et al., 2019; Elovitz et al., 2019; Hočevar et al., 2019; Chang et al., 2020; Odogwu et al., 2021; Kumar et al., 2021; Dunlop et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple microbiome studies.

claim: Reduced vaginal concentrations of β-defensin-2 are associated with vaginal CST IV and sPTB.
source: Similar to SLPI, reduced vaginal concentrations of β-defensin-2 are associated with vaginal CST IV and sPTB (Elovitz et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: VEGF is one member of a family of pro-angiogenic, pro-vasculogenic growth factors with mild immunobiological functions including hematopoiesis.
source: VEGF is one member of a family of pro-angiogenic, pro-vasculogenic growth factors with mild immunobiological functions including hematopoiesis (Gerber and Ferrara, 2003; Gerber et al., 2002) and vascular permeability (Chen et al., 2012; Lal et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on VEGF function and established knowledge.

claim: Disruption of VEGF proteins and their receptors is largely implicated in diseases associated with vascular malformations including obstetrical diseases such as preeclampsia.
source: Indeed, disruption of VEGF proteins and their receptors is largely implicated in diseases associated with vascular malformations including obstetrical diseases such as preeclampsia (Tarca et al., 2019; Tarca et al., 2022; Chaiworapongsa et al., 2004), a known etiology of iatrogenic preterm birth (Goldenberg et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on VEGF in preeclampsia.

claim: Vaginal concentrations of VEGF were negatively correlated with Gemella spp. in women who went on to experience preterm birth.
source: Yet, more recently, we showed that vaginal concentrations of VEGF were negatively correlated with Gemella spp. in women who went on to experience preterm birth (Florova et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a prior study by the authors.

claim: The prevalence of sPTL or PPROM was higher among women with a history of sPTB.
source: As expected (Goldenberg et al., 2008), the prevalence of sPTL or PPROM was higher among women with a history of sPTB.
evidence: This is supported by demographic data in Table 1 and a citation to a review article.

claim: The study population represents the largest survey of the vaginal immunoproteome in a population at high risk for sPTB.
source: Hence, the current study represents the largest survey of the vaginal immunoproteome in a population at high risk for sPTB.
evidence: This is an inference based on the study design and sample size described.

claim: One-third of immune mediators showed an association with gestational age in normal pregnancy.
source: Importantly, one-third of these mediators showed an association with gestational age (Figure 2; Figure 2—source data 1 and 2), whereas the remaining were unaffected (Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2 , Figure 2—source data 1 and 2 ).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2 and its supplements.

claim: The vaginal cytokine network in normal pregnancy is modestly modulated during gestation.
source: Together, these findings suggest that the vaginal cytokine network in normal pregnancy is modestly modulated during gestation, which prompted us to investigate whether a deviation from these changes occurs in women who ultimately undergo sPTB.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data showing specific changes in some but not all immune mediators during normal pregnancy.

claim: The majority of analytes displayed consistent change between sPTL and PPROM compared to controls.
source: Overall, the majority of analytes displayed consistent change between the two sPTB subsets, as demonstrated by positive correlation of fold changes (r = 0.87, p<0.0001).
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis data shown in Figure 6 supplement 1.

claim: VEGF and β-defensin-2 showed the largest decrease in sPTL and PPROM compared to controls.
source: VEGF and β-defensin-2 showed the largest decrease in sPTL and PPROM compared to controls, whereas CCL3, CCL4, and IL-6 displayed the largest increase.
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis data shown in Figure 6 supplement 1.

claim: CCL3, CCL4, and IL-6 displayed the largest increase in sPTL and PPROM compared to controls.
source: VEGF and β-defensin-2 showed the largest decrease in sPTL and PPROM compared to controls, whereas CCL3, CCL4, and IL-6 displayed the largest increase.
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis data shown in Figure 6 supplement 1.

claim: Specific immune mediators (CXCL10, SLPI, and LT-α) displayed differing directions of change between sPTL and PPROM.
source: Yet, specific immune mediators (CXCL10, SLPI, and LT-α) displayed differing directions of change between sPTL and PPROM.
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis data shown in Figure 6 supplement 1.

claim: sPTB cases share a common inflammatory profile; yet, subtle differences may allow the distinction of its subsets.
source: This finding indicates that sPTB cases share a common inflammatory profile; yet, subtle differences may allow the distinction of its subsets.
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation analysis showing both similarities and differences between sPTL and PPROM.

claim: IL-6, CCL2, CCL3, CCL4, and VEGF were shown to have a significant interaction between the disease outcome for sPTL and PPROM and for gestational age.
source: IL-6, CCL2, CCL3, CCL4, and VEGF were shown to have a significant interaction between the disease outcome for sPTL and PPROM and for gestational age (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling with interaction terms shown in Figure 6 supplement 2.

claim: IL-1β was the only immune mediator that had a significant interaction term (increased trend) for sPTL but not PPROM.
source: Notably, IL-1β was the only immune mediator that had a significant interaction term (increased trend) for sPTL but not PPROM (Figure 6—figure supplement 2), whereas no mediators were significant for PPROM but not sPTL.
evidence: This claim is supported by linear mixed effects modeling with interaction terms shown in Figure 6 supplement 2.

claim: The combination of immunoproteomic data and maternal characteristics resulted in significantly increased prediction of PPROM <30 (DeLong test p<0.04).
source: Likewise, the combination of immunoproteomic data and maternal characteristics resulted in higher point estimates than maternal characteristics alone for all outcomes considered, and significantly increased prediction of PPROM <30 (DeLong test p<0.04), when using the last sample before 24 weeks (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by predictive modeling data shown in Figure 7 supplement 1E.

claim: The vaginal immunoproteome and cervical length provide comparable predictive value for early PPROM.
source: As shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2, the vaginal immunoproteome and cervical length provide comparable predictive value for early PPROM; yet, cervical length alone was a better predictor of sPTB than the vaginal immunoproteome.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of predictive models shown in Figure 7 supplement 2.

claim: Cervical length alone was a better predictor of sPTB than the vaginal immunoproteome.
source: As shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2, the vaginal immunoproteome and cervical length provide comparable predictive value for early PPROM; yet, cervical length alone was a better predictor of sPTB than the vaginal immunoproteome.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of predictive models shown in Figure 7 supplement 2.

claim: For early PPROM, adding the immunoproteome data to cervical length increased the AUC point estimate from AUC = 0.727 (0.597–0.857) to AUC = 0.797 (0.678–0.917).
source: Notably, for early PPROM, adding the immunoproteome data to cervical length increased the AUC point estimate from AUC = 0.727 (0.597–0.857) to AUC = 0.797 (0.678–0.917) (Figure 7—figure supplement 2E), suggesting that the incorporation of the vaginal immune response into predictive screening may bolster the strength of these models.
evidence: This claim is supported by predictive modeling data shown in Figure 7 supplement 2E.

claim: The vaginal immunoproteome analyzed during the second trimester can generate noninvasive biomarkers with potential predictive value for early preterm birth cases.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrate that the vaginal immunoproteome analyzed during the second trimester can generate noninvasive biomarkers with potential predictive value for early preterm birth cases, although the clinical utility of such models needs to be investigated further.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the predictive modeling results presented in Figure 7 and its supplements.

claim: The vaginal immunoproteome has improved predictive value over maternal characteristics alone for a subset of early sPTB.
source: Regardless, these data show that the vaginal immunoproteome has improved predictive value over maternal characteristics alone for a subset of early sPTB, highlighting that vaginal immune mediator changes in a subset of preterm birth are attributable to factors other than maternal characteristics.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of predictive models with and without maternal characteristics shown in Figure 7.

claim: The vaginal ecosystem includes cellular and soluble components that maintain homeostasis and provide defense against potential pathogens.
source: The vaginal ecosystem includes cellular and soluble components that maintain homeostasis and provide defense against potential pathogens (Donders et al., 2003; Lee et al., 2015; Smith and Ravel, 2017; Mei et al., 2019; Hezelgrave et al., 2020; Monin et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to review articles and established knowledge.

claim: The soluble fraction of the vaginal ecosystem includes cytokines, chemokines, antimicrobial peptides/proteins, metabolites, antibodies, and complement components.
source: The soluble fraction includes cytokines, chemokines, antimicrobial peptides/proteins, metabolites, antibodies, and complement components, among others, (Donders et al., 2003; Wei et al., 2010; Tribe, 2015; Oh et al., 2019; Pruski et al., 2021; Delgado-Diaz et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies characterizing vaginal soluble components.

claim: The maternal-fetal interface undergoes three inflammatory phases: a pro-inflammatory profile accompanies the process of implantation, an anti-inflammatory state is maintained throughout the majority of gestation, and an inflammatory milieu is associated with the onset of parturition.
source: It is likely that the vaginal soluble fraction mirrors the three inflammatory phases described at the maternal-fetal interface: a pro-inflammatory profile accompanies the process of implantation, an anti-inflammatory state is maintained throughout the majority of gestation, and an inflammatory milieu is associated with the onset of parturition (Gomez-Lopez et al., 2010; Erlebacher, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to review articles describing inflammatory phases at the maternal-fetal interface.

claim: The vaginal soluble fraction likely mirrors the three inflammatory phases described at the maternal-fetal interface.
source: It is likely that the vaginal soluble fraction mirrors the three inflammatory phases described at the maternal-fetal interface: a pro-inflammatory profile accompanies the process of implantation, an anti-inflammatory state is maintained throughout the majority of gestation, and an inflammatory milieu is associated with the onset of parturition (Gomez-Lopez et al., 2010; Erlebacher, 2013).
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on inference from known inflammatory phases at the maternal-fetal interface.

claim: Immune homeostasis is required to maintain a successful pregnancy until delivery.
source: Our results are consistent with the prevailing hypothesis that immune homeostasis is required to maintain a successful pregnancy until delivery, and that a breakdown of such homeostasis is implicated as a mechanism of disease for sPTB (Gomez-Lopez et al., 2020; Gomez-Lopez et al., 2021; Gomez-Lopez et al., 2022a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to review articles and is consistent with established knowledge in the field.

claim: A breakdown of immune homeostasis is implicated as a mechanism of disease for sPTB.
source: Our results are consistent with the prevailing hypothesis that immune homeostasis is required to maintain a successful pregnancy until delivery, and that a breakdown of such homeostasis is implicated as a mechanism of disease for sPTB (Gomez-Lopez et al., 2020; Gomez-Lopez et al., 2021; Gomez-Lopez et al., 2022a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to review articles and is consistent with established knowledge in the field.

claim: Systems biology approaches using proteomics, cytomics, and transcriptomics have conceptualized an immunological clock for pregnancy.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, systems biology approaches using proteomics, cytomics, and transcriptomics have conceptualized an immunological clock for pregnancy and have suggested that the early detection of its malfunction may allow for the prediction of sPTB (Aghaeepour et al., 2017; Aghaeepour et al., 2018; Gomez-Lopez et al., 2019c; Ghaemi et al., 2019; Peterson et al., 2020; Tarca et al., 2021; Stelzer et al., 2021; Gomez-Lopez et al., 2022b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple systems biology studies.

claim: The early detection of malfunction in the immunological clock may allow for the prediction of sPTB.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, systems biology approaches using proteomics, cytomics, and transcriptomics have conceptualized an immunological clock for pregnancy and have suggested that the early detection of its malfunction may allow for the prediction of sPTB (Aghaeepour et al., 2017; Aghaeepour et al., 2018; Gomez-Lopez et al., 2019c; Ghaemi et al., 2019; Peterson et al., 2020; Tarca et al., 2021; Stelzer et al., 2021; Gomez-Lopez et al., 2022b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple systems biology studies.

claim: The elevated vaginal concentrations of IL-6 and IL-1β may point to a local inflammatory response that precedes intra-amniotic inflammation that is conventionally associated with sPTB.
source: Thus, given their stereotypical role in acute inflammation, the elevated vaginal concentrations of IL-6 and IL-1β described herein may therefore point to a local inflammatory response that precedes intra-amniotic inflammation that is conventionally associated with sPTB.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the data showing elevated IL-6 and IL-1β in women who later developed sPTB.

claim: Women destined to undergo sPTL and PPROM share a common signature of monocyte recruitment prior to disease onset.
source: These data suggest that women destined to undergo sPTL and PPROM share a common signature of monocyte recruitment prior to disease onset; indeed, such infiltrating cells may represent a source of the acute vaginal cytokine response (i.e., elevated concentrations of IL-6 and IL-1β) that was also observed herein.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data showing increased monocyte chemokines in women with sPTB.

claim: Infiltrating monocytes may represent a source of the acute vaginal cytokine response observed in sPTB.
source: These data suggest that women destined to undergo sPTL and PPROM share a common signature of monocyte recruitment prior to disease onset; indeed, such infiltrating cells may represent a source of the acute vaginal cytokine response (i.e., elevated concentrations of IL-6 and IL-1β) that was also observed herein.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the observed increase in both monocyte chemokines and pro-inflammatory cytokines.

claim: The vaginal ecosystem of women who are destined to undergo early PPROM displays a suppressed AMP-driven host response.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that the vaginal ecosystem of women who are destined to undergo early PPROM displays a suppressed AMP-driven host response; however, additional research is required to determine whether this decrease reflects an impaired or a dampened response.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data showing decreased SLPI and β-defensin-2 in early PPROM.

claim: A hostile vaginal milieu may lead to reduced VEGF levels and functions, such as angiogenesis, which could be implicated with early preterm birth regardless of the process of membrane rupture.
source: In the context of previous studies, our data suggest that a hostile vaginal milieu may lead to reduced VEGF levels and functions, such as angiogenesis, which could be implicated with early preterm birth regardless of the process of membrane rupture.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the data showing decreased VEGF in both sPTL and PPROM cases.

claim: The assessment of the immune response and its interactions with the microbiome could be considered together with other prenatal screening tools to construct a comprehensive minimally invasive screening tool for preterm birth.
source: Nonetheless, our results as well as those of previous studies suggest that the assessment of the immune response and its interactions with the microbiome (Fettweis et al., 2019; Flaviani et al., 2021; Florova et al., 2021; Elovitz et al., 2019) could be considered together with other prenatal screening tools to construct a comprehensive minimally invasive screening tool for preterm birth.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the current study's findings and citations to prior studies showing the value of combined approaches.

claim: Only 1–2% of pregnant mothers have the clinical finding of a sonographic short cervix in a mid-trimester transvaginal ultrasound screening.
source: Furthermore, only 1–2% of pregnant mothers have the clinical finding of a sonographic short cervix in a mid-trimester transvaginal ultrasound screening (Fonseca et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a clinical study.

claim: Among women with short cervix, selective administration of vaginal progesterone will reduce the risk of delivery before 37 weeks by half.
source: Among these women, selective administration of vaginal progesterone will reduce the risk of delivery before 37 weeks by half (Fonseca et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a clinical trial.

claim: Self-swabbing is now considered an effective way of vaginal fluid collection.
source: An advantage of vaginal sampling is that self-swabbing is now considered an effective way of vaginal fluid collection (Haguenoer et al., 2014; Lunny et al., 2015); therefore, a screening tool based on vaginal biomarkers may be developed for use in low-resource areas with a scarcity of healthcare providers.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on self-collection methods.

claim: The vaginal immunoproteome undergoes homeostatic changes throughout gestation and deviations from this shift are associated with sPTB.
source: The vaginal immunoproteome undergoes homeostatic changes throughout gestation and deviations from this shift are associated with sPTB.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the data presented throughout the manuscript showing gestational age-dependent changes in normal pregnancy and alterations in sPTB cases.

claim: The vaginal immunoproteome can be leveraged as a potential biomarker for early sPTB, a subset of sPTB associated with extremely adverse neonatal outcomes.
source: Furthermore, the vaginal immunoproteome can be leveraged as a potential biomarker for early sPTB, a subset of sPTB associated with extremely adverse neonatal outcomes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the predictive modeling results and established knowledge about outcomes of early preterm birth.
